title: Avalanche Intelligence Platform
tagline: Machine learning and geospatial analysis for avalanche terrain awareness.
summary: An AI-based platform that combines terrain models, satellite data and weather inputs to analyze avalanche-prone terrain and present the results on an interactive map.
problem: Avalanche risk depends on many interacting factors: slope angle, aspect, elevation, recent snowfall, wind loading and temperature. That information is spread across terrain models, satellite imagery and weather feeds in different formats and resolutions, which makes it hard to bring together into one clear, location-specific picture of where terrain is most susceptible.
solution: A Python data pipeline that ingests a Digital Elevation Model (DEM) and satellite data, derives terrain features such as slope, aspect and curvature, and combines them with weather variables. Supervised machine learning models (Random Forest and Support Vector Machine) are trained to classify terrain susceptibility, and the results are rendered as layers on an interactive web map so they can be explored visually.

architecture.overview: The system is organised as a batch processing pipeline feeding a lightweight API and a map-based frontend. Heavy geospatial computation happens offline; the web layer only serves pre-computed results.

features.title: Terrain feature extraction
features.description: Derives slope angle, aspect and curvature from elevation data, which are the core terrain variables used in avalanche assessment.

features.title: Satellite data integration
features.description: Brings satellite-derived information into the same spatial grid as the terrain model so every location has a consistent set of features.

features.title: ML susceptibility classification
features.description: Trains and compares Random Forest and SVM models to classify terrain into susceptibility categories.

features.title: Interactive risk map
features.description: Displays model output as toggleable map layers with a clear legend, so results can be explored by location.

challenges.title: Aligning heterogeneous data
challenges.description: DEMs, satellite rasters and weather data come with different resolutions, projections and time stamps. Aligning them correctly onto one grid is a core part of the work.

challenges.title: Limited and imbalanced labels
challenges.description: Recorded avalanche events are rare compared with stable terrain, which makes training data imbalanced and requires careful evaluation rather than relying on a single accuracy number.

challenges.title: Communicating uncertainty
challenges.description: Model outputs are a decision-support aid, not a safety guarantee. The interface needs to communicate that clearly.

learnings: Working with raster geospatial data, coordinate reference systems and reprojection
Choosing evaluation metrics suited to imbalanced classification
Designing pipelines that separate heavy offline processing from a fast web layer

title: AI Business Automation Agent
tagline: An AI agent that runs business workflows, connects APIs and produces reports.
summary: An AI agent architecture that takes routine business tasks, such as gathering data from connected services, processing it and producing structured reports, and automates them end to end with logging and human review.
problem: Small teams spend significant time on repetitive operational work: copying data between tools, compiling status updates, summarising information and preparing recurring reports. The work is necessary but low-leverage, and doing it by hand is slow and error-prone.
solution: An agent built around a large language model that can plan a task, call a defined set of tools (API integrations, data processing functions, report generators) and assemble the results. Workflows are triggered on a schedule or by events, every step is logged, and outputs can be held for human review before they are sent.

architecture.overview: A Python service hosts the agent loop. The LLM decides which tool to call next; each tool is a small, tested Python function with a strict input schema. A workflow layer handles triggers, retries and logging.

features.title: Tool-calling agent
features.description: The LLM selects from a defined set of tools with validated inputs instead of producing free-form actions.

features.title: API integrations
features.description: Connectors for external services let the agent read and write data where the business already works.

features.title: Intelligent reporting
features.description: Collected data is summarised into structured, readable reports generated automatically.

features.title: Logging & human review
features.description: Every run is logged step by step, and sensitive outputs can require approval before they are sent.

challenges.title: Reliability of LLM output
challenges.description: LLMs can produce inconsistent output. Strict tool schemas, validation and retries are needed to keep the workflow predictable.

challenges.title: Safe tool access
challenges.description: An agent should only have the permissions a task requires. Scoping credentials and actions is part of the design.

challenges.title: Cost and latency
challenges.description: Each model call costs time and money, so workflows have to be designed to use the model only where it adds value.

learnings: Designing tool interfaces that LLMs can use reliably
Building observable automation with logs and review steps
Integrating multiple third-party APIs behind a consistent internal interface

title: AI-Enabled Car Sales Platform
tagline: A full-stack dealership platform with lead management and business automation.
summary: A full-stack web application for a car sales business: vehicle listings, customer inquiries captured as leads, a lead management dashboard and automation that helps the sales team respond faster.
problem: Smaller car dealerships often manage inventory and customer inquiries across spreadsheets, phone calls and messaging apps. Leads get lost, follow-ups are inconsistent and there is little visibility into where each potential buyer is in the sales process.
solution: A Flask web application with a public vehicle catalogue and inquiry forms that feed directly into a lead management system. Staff get a dashboard to track lead status, and automation handles repetitive steps such as lead notifications, follow-up reminders and AI-assisted inquiry summaries.

architecture.overview: A server-rendered Flask application backed by a relational database, with background automation jobs and optional AI services for working with inquiry text.

features.title: Vehicle catalogue
features.description: Searchable listings with detail pages so customers can browse available inventory.

features.title: Lead capture
features.description: Inquiry and test-drive forms create structured lead records automatically instead of scattered messages.

features.title: Lead management dashboard
features.description: Staff can see every lead, its status and its history in one place.

features.title: Sales automation
features.description: Automatic notifications and follow-up reminders reduce the chance of a lead being forgotten.

challenges.title: Modelling the sales pipeline
challenges.description: Lead stages and status transitions need to match how a dealership actually works, which shapes the data model.

challenges.title: Useful, not intrusive, automation
challenges.description: Reminders and notifications should help staff without creating noise or spamming customers.

challenges.title: Data quality
challenges.description: Form validation and duplicate handling keep the lead database clean and trustworthy.

learnings: Structuring a Flask application with clear separation of routes, models and services
Designing relational data models for a real business process
Applying automation to a concrete sales workflow
